design_loop.goal: Verify nominal geometric fit of the 235 mm source-bound bench carrier, supports and explicit battery/wire installation volumes in the 250 mm bay. Record only static model fit; exclude hardware, thermal and flight qualification.

attempts.title: Final source-bound bay with wire service envelopes

findings: Reviewed current isometric and rear elevation renderings for the connected carrier, battery and converter supports and wire-service reservations.
The models show conservative component bounds and empty service reservations, not a detailed production wiring harness.

checks.finding: One carrier assembly stands between the two circular bulkheads. Battery, converter and service volumes are distinct attached bodies.
The long narrow 235 mm PCB and 242 mm carrier match the 250 mm bay; the 68 mm battery reservation occupies less than a third of the length.
Rear views show the battery tray, rear converter, eight pass-through positions, two terminal-service cross regions and both side cable corridors.
Visible purchased-part bounds and service volumes attach to the continuous carrier/PCB assembly; no detached object appears outside the bay assembly.
The battery rests against the tray and end stops; the converter aligns with its support bars. Rails capture the PCB edges. Actual retention and assembly tolerances remain measured hardware gates.
The model is Z-up, with the aft bulkhead at the bottom and forward eyelet above. Battery and converter sit on the rear side; the switch projects radially.
The isometric and -Y elevation show the same rear battery, upper connector reservation, lower converter and lateral corridors without an unexplained orientation change.
